item.title: Hypersurfaces with Non-diagonalizable Shape Operators in Minkowski Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study hypersurfaces $M^4$ in the Minkowski space $\mathbb{E}^5_1$ whose shape operator $S$ is non-diagonalizable, having a triple real eigenvalue $\lambda$ with a one-dimensional eigenspace together with a simple eigenvalue $\mu$ (Case~(iii) in the classification of Magid). Assuming that $\lambda$ and $\mu$ satisfy a functional relation $\lambda=f(\mu)$ and that the eigenvector field of $\mu$ is geodesic, we show that $\lambda$ and $\mu$, as well as the pseudo-orthonormal frame, are intrinsic invariants of $M$, determined by the induced metric up to sign. As a consequence, we prove that such hypersurfaces are unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{E}^5_1$. We also obtain a classification of the warped product hypersurfaces of this type.
item.dc:creator: Z\"ulal Derin Yaqub, Nurettin Cenk Turgay

item.title: Rigidity of Three-Dimensional Self-Shrinkers with Constant Norm of the Second Fundamental Form
item.description: arXiv:2610.18947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X:M^3\to\R^4$ be a complete, connected self-shrinker without boundary, and suppose that the squared norm $S$ of its second fundamental form is constant. We prove that $S=0$ or $S=1$. Accordingly, the image is a hyperplane through the origin or a generalized cylinder $\mathbb S^k(\sqrt{k})\times\R^{3-k}$, $1\le k\le3$, and the immersion is a Riemannian covering onto its image.
item.dc:creator: Shanlin Guan, Yuhang Zhao

item.title: Panopticum of 3D snake models
item.description: arXiv:2610.19036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the standard 2-dimensional 3-segment snake model, leading to the famous $(2,3,5)$ geometry, we discuss a series of 3-dimensional models of similar snakes. In particular, we seek for rules allowing to steer them exclusively by the two joints, which expects 4-dimensional control freedom. This leads to interesting $(4,9)$ and $(4,10)$ models. Finally, we discuss modifications of the previous snakes which lead to $(4,8)$ models. All of the models open further questions and should be a good baseline for further research.
item.dc:creator: Martin Dole\v{z}al, Jan Slov\'{a}k

item.title: Existence of exhaustions with controlled sign of mean curvature in noncompact manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.19241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a complete and non-compact Riemannian manifold of dimension $3\le n\le 7$, we find conditions for the existence of compact exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ such that all boundaries $\partial U_i$ have the same sign of mean curvature. In particular, we show that in these dimensions, a manifold with one end satisfying a no tentacle condition always has a weakly mean convex, weakly mean concave, or minimal exhaustion, according to the behaviour of the area profile of separating hypersurfaces. This is a version of a result sketched by Gromov, under a condition which is weaker than his thickness at infinity. In more general situations, we study the existence of exhaustions which are weakly mean concave or weakly mean convex apart from an arbitrarily small $L^1$ error. That is, we find sufficient conditions for the existence of exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ which satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}H^+\to0$, $\int_{\partial U_i}H^-\to0$, or $\int_{\partial U_i}|H|\to0$, where $H^-$, $H^+$, and $|H|$ are the negative part, positive part, and the absolute value of the mean curvature respectively. As an application of our methods, we study the existence of almost $c$-convex exhaustions, that is, exhaustions whose boundaries satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}(H-c)^-\to0$ for some $c>0$.
item.dc:creator: Anushree Das

item.title: Long-Time Behavior of the $\alpha$-Ricci Flow on the 2-Torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.19273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the $\alpha$-Ricci flow $(g(t),\alpha(t))$, which is a Ricci flow coupled with a harmonic 1-form heat flow, on the 2-torus $M$. We prove global existence for this flow as well as a Type III curvature estimate. The long-time behavior of the $\alpha$-Ricci flow depends on the cohomology class $[\alpha] \in H^1(M,\mathbb{R})$, which is invariant under the flow. If $[\alpha]$ is rational, then as $t\to\infty$, $(M,t^{-1}g(t))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to $S^1$ with length $\ell([\alpha])/\sqrt 2$ where $\ell([\alpha])$ is the primitive length of $[\alpha]$. On the universal cover, the rescaled flow $(s^{-1}\tilde g(st),\tilde\alpha(st))$ smoothly converges to an expander $(g^*(t),\alpha^*(t))$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ as $s\to \infty$ where $\alpha^*(t)$ is nonzero and constant in spacetime and $g^*(t)$ is flat and expanding in the $\alpha^*$ direction. If $[\alpha]$ is irrational, then there is a sequence $s_i\to\infty$ such that $(M,s_i^{-1}g(s_it))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to a point. Moreover, on the universal cover, $(s_i^{-1}\tilde g(s_it),\tilde\alpha(s_it))$ smoothly converges to $(g^*(t),\alpha^*(t))$.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Guo, Xiaokang Wang

item.title: Calabi metric on the space of k-Hessian potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.19653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $1\leq k\leq n$. We consider the space of smooth $k$-admissible potentials introduced in the study of the Hessian-cscK equation by Guo--Smith--Tong. The complex $k$-Hessian equation identifies this space, modulo constants, with the space of smooth positive densities of fixed total mass. We compute the differential of the Hessian density map and use it to pull back the Fisher--Rao metric. The resulting Riemannian metric is \[ G^{\HC,k}_{\varphi}(u,v) =\int_X \bigl(\Delta_{\varphi}^{(k)}u\bigr) \bigl(\Delta_{\varphi}^{(k)}v\bigr) \,\omega_{\varphi}^{k}\wedge\omega^{n-k}. \] We then show that the square-root Hessian density map \[ \varphi\longmapsto 2\sqrt{\frac{\omega_{\varphi}^{k}\wedge\omega^{n-k}}{\omega^n}} \] is a global Riemannian isometry onto the positive part of the $L^2(X,\omega^n)$-sphere of radius $2\sqrt{V}$, where $V=\int_X\omega^n$. For $k=n$, this recovers the spherical description of the classical Calabi metric. We also derive the curvature, geodesic and diameter formulas, and prove a quantitative local comparison between adjacent Hessian--Fisher distances.
item.dc:creator: Linwei Zhang

item.title: The fence conjecture for convex projective polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.19664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the fence conjecture of Dumas and Wolf: for a convex projective polygon with at least five vertices, every zero of the Pick differential lies in the interior of the region obtained by cutting off the triangles at consecutive triples of vertices. The proof gives a stronger estimate for arbitrary properly convex domains. In affine-sphere coordinates normalized at a Pick zero, the domain contains the closed disk of radius $2^{-1/4}$ and its closure lies in the open disk of radius $2^{1/4}$, unless it is a rotated square. The proof compares the canonical Monge-Amp\`ere potential of the domain with that of a normalized square. Their third-order contact gives alternating local sign sectors. A planar separation argument and the maximum principle show that the negative sectors belong to four distinct components, each meeting a different side of the square. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.
item.dc:creator: Erxiao Wang

item.title: Remarks on prescribed scalar curvature functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.19667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This short article is devoted to the study of the positive solution of Yamabe-type semi-linear equation with prescribed coefficient on general closed manifolds. Our main result is to provide some sufficient conditions for the existence of the positive solutions and give some examples to show that those conditions are sharp. An application to scalar-flat manifold settles a long standing question in prescribing scalar curvature problem in negative form.
item.dc:creator: Mingxiang Li, Quoc Anh Ngo, Xingwang Xu

item.title: The Weil-Petersson diameter of moduli space for large genus
item.description: arXiv:2610.19707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the large-genus order of the Weil-Petersson diameter of $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ for each fixed number of punctures: namely, $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{M}_{g,n})\asymp\sqrt g\log g$. The main new ingredient is an integrated Ricci estimate for geodesics that minimize in moduli space and have thick endpoints, with no systole bound along their interiors.
item.dc:creator: Yunhui Wu

item.title: Coupled reciprocal-sum inequalities for Neumann eigenvalues in rank-one symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a rank-one symmetric space of compact or noncompact type and real dimension $m=kn$, where $k\in\{1,2,4,8\}$ is the real dimension of the underlying division algebra. Meng and Wang proved sharp isoperimetric inequalities for reciprocal sums of the first $p$ or $\ell$ nonzero Neumann eigenvalues, with indices strictly below $m$ in the nonconstant-curvature cases. We keep the whole $m$-dimensional transplanted first eigenspace of an equimeasurable geodesic ball and treat its mass and stiffness forms as a coupled generalized eigenvalue problem. For every bounded connected smooth domain in a noncompact rank-one symmetricspace we prove the full sharp estimate \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}\frac{1}{\mu_j(\Omega)} \ge \frac{m}{\mu_1(B)}, \] where $B$ is a geodesic ball with $|B|=|\Omega|$; equality characterizes geodesic balls. The Hopf-direction contribution is encoded by a positive, unital, trace-preserving projection on symmetric matrices, and the finite-dimensional closure is supplied by a positive-projection Jensen inequality. In compact type, under the localization hypothesis of Meng--Wang, the same full estimate is obtained whenever $\cot^2 R\ge k-1$, where $R$ is the radius of the comparison ball, as well as in the isotropic endpoint cases and for Hopf-balanced angular second moment. Consequently the complete $m$-term inequality holds for all complex and quaternionic projective spaces under the original localization assumption, and for the Cayley plane when $R\le \arctan(1/\sqrt7)$. In the remaining admissible Cayley interval we exhibit a finite-dimensional obstruction showing that the affine tangent-matrix bounds alone cannot yield the full trace estimate. This obstruction concerns the proof mechanism and is not a counterexample to the unresolved spectral inequality.
item.dc:creator: Yifeng Meng

item.title: A parabolic flow approach to generalized Gauduchon metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.19887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a parabolic proof of the Fu-Wang-Wu theorem for semilinear elliptic equations associated with generalized Gauduchon metrics. Fixing a Hermitian metric $\omega$, we introduce a flow $\partial_t v-\Delta v=\psi(\vert\nabla v\vert^2)+\langle B,dv\rangle-c(t)-f(x)$ for the conformal factor, whose stationary points solve the semilinear elliptic equation of Fu-Wang-Wu. Under the growth condition $\liminf_{t\to+\infty}\psi(t)/t^\mu>0$ for some $\mu>\tfrac{1}{2}$, we prove that the flow exists uniquely for all time and converges; the limit solves the elliptic equation and is unique up to addition of a constant. Our convergence argument does not rely on a gradient-flow structure or a monotone energy functional. In particular, this recovers, by a flow method rather than the continuity method, the existence and uniqueness theorem of Fu-Wang-Wu on $k$-th generalized Gauduchon metrics, providing a new parabolic approach to their elliptic theory.
item.dc:creator: Han Luo

item.title: Algebraic and Symmetrized Affine star-Ricci Solitons for the Bott Connection on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.20042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We fix a spacelike two-dimensional left-invariant distribution and its associated almost contact structure on a three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie group, and investigate the star-Ricci contraction of the curvature of the Bott connection. We compute the complete tensor for seven standard bracket families and determine all real parameter solutions of the general algebraic equation and its self-adjoint subclass. Using the symmetric part of the tensor, we also define a Bott affine star-Ricci soliton equation and classify all left-invariant vector field solutions. Every affine solution is steady, while two non-unimodular families admit branches with a nonzero symmetrized tensor. The proofs provide complete component equations, treat all degenerate parameter branches, and establish sufficiency by explicit substitution. We also distinguish almost contact structures from contact metric structures.
item.dc:creator: Yuxin Ding

item.title: A semi-discrete scheme for horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.20054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The horizontal mean curvature flow is a geometric evolution associated with the horizontal perimeter in sub-Riemannian spaces. In this paper, we introduce a minimizing movement scheme for this flow in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}$, and prove the existence of a flat flow which is locally $1/2$-H\"older continuous in time, with respect to the $L^1$-distance. The construction applies to arbitrary bounded sets of finite horizontal perimeter and does not require smoothness or symmetry of the initial datum.
item.dc:creator: A. Cesaroni, M. Novaga, P. Pozzi

item.title: Ball growth at all scales in universal covers of short metric graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected metric graph of first Betti number $b\ge 2$, and let $\Gamma_b$ be a trivalent graph of the same Betti number with all edges of unit length. We show that if $\text{length}(\Gamma) \le \lambda\, \text{length}(\Gamma_b)$, then the universal cover of $\Gamma$ contains a vertex around which, \emph{at every radius} $R\ge 0$, the ball is at least as long as the ball of radius $R$ in the trivalent tree whose edges all have length $3\lambda$. In particular, for $\lambda\le\frac13$, this ball is at least as long as the ball of the same radius in the universal cover of $\Gamma_b$, with no multiplicative loss. This improves an earlier theorem of the author, which gives the weaker lower bound $(1-3\lambda)$ times the ball in the universal cover of $\Gamma_b$, and only for $\lambda\le\frac16$. The proof rests on an elementary comparison principle. Among trees whose vertices have degree at least three and whose edges have length at most $c$, the trivalent tree with all edges of length $c$ has the smallest balls at every radius. As an application, we double the exponential growth rate in the author's earlier uniform lower bound for the area of balls in the universal cover of small-area surfaces of hyperbolic type, from $\ln 2$ to $2\ln 2$, beyond the hyperbolic rate. We also obtain explicit constants in the positive answer to Guth's question for surfaces. Finally, we conjecture the sharp, all-scale version of the minimal volume entropy inequality of Kapovich--Nagnibeda and Lim, and show that it would be optimal.
item.dc:creator: Steve Karam

item.title: On the generalized cohomologies of almost abelian solvmanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalized complex structures give rise to generalized Dolbeault, Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomologies. We study these cohomologies for invariant generalized complex structures on almost abelian Lie algebras $\mathfrak g_A=\mathbb R e_0\ltimes_A\mathfrak h$, where $\mathfrak h$ is an abelian ideal of codimension one, and on almost abelian solvmanifolds $\Gamma\backslash G_A$. We first show that the invariant generalized Dolbeault cohomology can be identified with the Chevalley--Eilenberg cohomology of the complex Lie algebra $\mathcal L$, the $+{\mathbf i}$-eigenspace of the structure, with coefficients in a character determined by the canonical line. We prove that $\mathcal L$ is itself an almost abelian Lie algebra; thus the cohomology reduces to the kernel and cokernel of an explicit derivation. Assuming that $A$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb R$, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the cohomology dimensions and compare with compact quotients. Other comparison results are discussed, noting that the cohomology of invariant forms always injects into that of $\Gamma\backslash G_A$.
item.dc:creator: Mauro de Andrade Pinto, Let\'icia Campon\^es do Brasil Maia, Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins

item.title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $\alpha$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.
item.dc:creator: Kewei Li

item.title: Invariant complex structures on the Euclidean motion group as deformations of Calabi-Eckmann structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify, up to equivalence, all left-invariant complex structures on the three-dimensional Euclidean rigid motion group $SE(3).$ Our approach is based on the correspondence between complex structures on a real Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}(3)$ of the motion group and complex Lie subalgebras of the complexification of $\mathfrak{e}(3).$ The resulting structures form a one-parameter family $J_\phi.$ We further establish a connection with the classical Calabi-Eckmann complex structures on $S^3\times S^3.$ More precisely, we construct a one-parameter deformation of Lie brackets connecting $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus \mathfrak{so}(3)$ to $\mathfrak{e}(3),$ for which each endomorphism $J_\phi$ remains integrable. Consequently, every left-invariant complex structure on $SE(3)$ arises as a contraction limit of Calabi-Eckmann structures. The same family of endomorphisms also defines complex structures on $\mathfrak{so}(3,1).$
item.dc:creator: Neda Bokan, Srdjan Vukmirovic

item.title: Geometric $C^1$-stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.20265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow in the simply connected space forms under genuinely first-order geometric assumptions. The initial hypersurface is required to lie in a sufficiently thin annulus around a geodesic sphere and to have outward normal making a small angle with the radial direction. No convexity, mean convexity, initial curvature bound, or H\"older control of the normal is assumed. The main ingredient is a quantitative Alexandrov reflection argument that converts these initial assumptions into a strong reflection property preserved by the flow. The resulting radial and angular control allows us to derive estimates for the mean curvature and the full second fundamental form, and hence long-time existence, eventual convexity, and smooth exponential convergence to a geodesic sphere. In hyperbolic space, the eventual convexity can be strengthened to horospherical convexity. The reflection threshold also yields a quantitative estimate for the displacement of the limiting centre. For Lipschitz initial hypersurfaces, we develop a separate positive-time curvature estimate that is uniform along smooth approximations. This produces an instantaneously smooth evolution with the same eventual convexity and smooth exponential convergence.
item.dc:creator: Esther Cabezas-Rivas, Carlo Sinestrari

item.title: Odd mapping cone Chern character
item.description: arXiv:2610.20300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our previous work established the mapping cone Chern character on the even-degree side, using the powers of the mapping cone curvature associated with the given mapping cone connection. In this paper, we carry out the odd-degree version using a trivial mapping cone connection and an automorphism on a trivial complex vector bundle. This version is based on the related odd-degree transgression.
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhuang

item.title: CMC foliations on Euclidean spaces are minimal foliations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we provide a complete answer to one of the most classical conjectures in differential geometry (of foliations). More precisely, we present a complete positive answer to the classical conjecture, due to Meeks III, P\'erez, and Ros (2008), that states that every foliation on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ by (possibly varying) CMC hypersurfaces is a foliation by minimal hypersurfaces. Moreover, if $n\leq 6$, such a CMC foliation must consist of parallel hyperplanes.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio, Euripedes Carvalho da Silva

item.title: K-area bounds for smooth sphere bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.20440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E\to B$ be a smooth $S^n$ bundle with oriented Riemannian total space $(E,g)$, where $n\ge2$. We prove K-area$(E,g)\le4\pi n(n-1)/\sigma$ whenever every fibre has intrinsic scalar curvature at least $\sigma>0$, independently of the dimension of $B$. In particular, unit round fibres give K-area$(E,g)\le4\pi$. For arbitrary metrics on two-sphere fibres, K-area is bounded by the supremum of their areas. We also obtain stronger bounds from fibrewise scalar spectra.
item.dc:creator: Haoxuan Cheng

item.title: Allen--Cahn and mean curvature flows from Clifford hypersurfaces to equators
item.description: arXiv:2610.20453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note, using OpenAI's resolution of the Solomon--Yau conjecture, we extend our joint work with Pedro Gaspar to all dimensions $n\geq2$. We construct eternal Allen--Cahn flows on $S^{n+1}$ connecting approximations of any prescribed least-area Clifford hypersurface and equatorial sphere. We also construct infinitely many eternal integral Brakke flows from least-area Clifford hypersurfaces to equatorial spheres.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Chen

item.title: Cheng's Theorem in the Spectral Setting
item.description: arXiv:2610.20485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a maximal diameter rigidity theorem for closed 3-dimensional Riemannian manifolds under a spectral lower bound for the Ricci curvature. We show that if $0<\gamma<2$, $K>0$ and $\lambda_1(-\gamma\Delta+\operatorname{Ric})\geq 2K$, then the optimal bound $\operatorname{diam}(M,g)\leq\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{K}}$ is attained if and only if (M,g) is isometric to the round 3-sphere of constant sectional curvature $K$.
item.dc:creator: Carolina Ruviaro

item.title: $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth approximation of mod $k$ integral cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.20499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every mod $k$ integral cycle $T$ of sufficiently high codimension in an oriented Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ can be approximated in flat norm by a cycle which is a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifold $\Sigma$ of nearly the same area, up to a singular set of codimension 5. If in addition $T$ belongs to a mod $k$ homology class admitting an embedded $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth manifold representative, then $\Sigma$ can be taken fully regular, up to the codimension one stratum of classical singularities. This extends the smooth approximation theory to cycles with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ in stable regimes. Moreover, we provide examples showing the impossibility of locally approximating minimizing cycles by smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifolds, even in homology classes with smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth representatives.
item.dc:creator: Gianmarco Caldini, Anna Skorobogatova

item.title: On Meeks' conjecture on disjoint minimal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study disjoint solution pairs $(u,D)$ to the minimal surface equation in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $u=0$ on $\partial D.$ A conjecture of W. Meeks states that at most two such pairs can exist in $\mathbb{R}^n.$ We confirm the conjecture in two complementary cases. For $n\in\{2,3,4,5,6\},$ we prove it under a superlinearity assumption. In dimension $n=2,$ we establish the result under a suitable sublinearity assumption. We also derive estimates on the asymptotic angle of domains supporting nontrivial solutions for $n\geq 3.$
item.dc:creator: Angelo Benedetti, Barbara Nelli

item.title: Proof of the Penrose Conjecture for Maximally Parameterized Initial Data Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.20559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the spacetime Penrose inequality for asymptotically flat initial data sets $(M^n,g,k)$ in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, under the dominant energy condition, for data admitting the 'maximally parameterized form' defined in equation (4.7). In this case, the second fundamental form $k$ is locally parameterized by $n(n+1)/2$ functions, giving the same formal local functional degrees of freedom as an arbitrary symmetric $2$-tensor. The proof is based on a new 1-parameter family of generalized Schoen-Yau identities and their gauge-invariant specialization, inspired by the generalized Jang framework of Bray-Khuri [8, 9]. For maximally parameterized data, these identities produce a Riemannian comparison metric \[ \bar g=g+\beta\otimes\beta \] with nonnegative scalar curvature $R_{\bar{g}} \geq 0$. Under a natural nondegeneracy condition (5.7) at the apparent horizon, the comparison metric admits a smooth minimal completion up to $\partial M^n$. Together with suitable asymptotic control, this reduces the Penrose inequality to its Riemannian counterpart. The all-dimensional conclusion uses the Riemannian Penrose theorem of Bi-Zhu [6], together with a minimizing enclosure argument that allows singular boundaries. More generally, in the spirit of [8, 9], we note that the Penrose conjecture follows whenever a certain system of PDEs (3.18) involving $k$ can be solved, in which case our new identity (3.15) immediately implies $R_{\bar{g}} \geq 0$. A natural problem is thus to regularize our degenerate system to prove a general existence theory, thereby proving the Penrose conjecture. Essentially, we believe this is what the OpenAI paper [27] posted last week on October 6, 2026 claims to have done.
item.dc:creator: Hubert Bray, Tuan Dolmen, Marcus Khuri, David Schmidt

item.title: Complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors in low dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors with complex Killing function $i\mu-\alpha$ on complete Riemannian surfaces, presenting an explicit list of all possible cases. We show that, contrary to previous statements in the literature, there exist complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors on Riemannian surfaces for which $\alpha\mu\not\equiv0$. We illustrate the classification by providing several explicit local, compact, and complete examples, including a complete example for which $\alpha\mu>0$ everywhere. We then move to three dimensions, proving that a spin-c Riemannian three-manifold admits a complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor with complex Killing function $i\mu-\alpha$ if and only if it is a $\mu$-exact trans-Sasakian manifold of type $(\alpha,\mu)$. In addition, we construct a geodesically incomplete Riemannian three-manifold equipped with a complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor for which neither $\mu$ nor $\alpha$ vanishes identically, and then prove that this is not possible if the characteristic vector field of the associated trans-Sasakian structure is complete. These results settle a conjecture by Gro{\ss}e and Nakad (Results in Mathematics, 2015) stating that on two- and three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds the complex Killing function of any complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor must be either globally real or globally imaginary.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Luis Carmona Jim\'enez, Alejandro Gil-Garc\'ia, C. S. Shahbazi

item.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.19037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,\Phi)$ corresponds to a representation $\rho$ of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$, then $(E,-\Phi)$ corresponds to $(\overline{\rho}^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $\eta\mapsto-\eta$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.
item.dc:creator: Krishnendu Gongopadhyay, Tathagata Nayak

item.title: A short open space curve of unit width
item.description: arXiv:2610.19585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we propose a curve to be a minimum of length among rectifiable, continuous curves of unit width in three-dimensional Euclidean space. We show that a previously conjectured minimizer of that problem is not of unit width, give the numerical derivation of a candidate family of unit width curves, prove that it admits a strict local minimum within that candidate family and that this minimum is of unit width and length $3.905124162243593\ldots$. The curve consists of eight straight segments, two cone geodesics, and three circular helices. Its parameters are specified by a uniquely isolated solution of the joining and stationarity equations. To establish unit width in every direction, we combine analytic estimates with interval arithmetic on a finite covering of the remaining directions. We conjecture that the curve is globally minimizing. We supplement this work with the programs used to identify the candidates, replicate the computer-assisted parts of our proof, as well as a formalization of our proof in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Tinko Sebastian Bartels, Dennis Kevin Choy, Ruixiang Wu, Tongxin Li

item.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures III: Unfoldings
item.description: arXiv:2610.20011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We prove theorem of existence for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves for one-parameter families. We prove theorem of completeness for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We also present unfoldings of foliated nonsingular varieties defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves in the language of functors of Artin rings which is the algebraic version of unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures. We identify first-order unfoldings and obstructions.
item.dc:creator: Chunghoon Kim

item.title: A note on the failure of Payne's inequality on manifolds with boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.20097v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that Payne's conjecture on the comparison between Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues and buckling eigenvalues does not hold on flat and hyperbolic cylindrical surfaces and on (round) hemispheres.
item.dc:creator: Davide Buoso, Vladimir Lotoreichik

item.title: The WKB Riemann-Hilbert Problem for the Painlev\'e I System
item.description: arXiv:2610.20123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we solve the direct monodromy problem for the Borel-summed $0$-parameter solution of Painlev\'e~I. Using the auxiliary time equation, we first construct formal WKB wave matrices whose amplitudes are regular at the double turning point. Rigorous Borel summation then yields exact WKB matrices in each Stokes region. Uniform estimates on moving action strips provide a common exact wave matrix in a full neighbourhood of the double point, proving that all four incident jumps are identities for consistent column normalisations. We formulate the resulting normalised Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its existence and uniqueness on the Borel domains of the construction. Finally, after Painlev\'e scaling, the five Borel-summed solutions coincide with the five rotated tritronqu\'ee solutions of Painlev\'e~I.
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Alameddine, Olivier Marchal, Nikita Nikolaev, Nicolas Orantin

item.title: Quantization of positive Lagrangians
item.description: arXiv:2610.20177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A Lagrangian submanifold in an almost Calabi-Yau manifold is called positive if the real part of the holomorphic volume form restricted to it is positive. It is called $\epsilon$-positive if the ratio of the restrictions of the imaginary and real parts of the holomorphic volume form is bounded by $\frac{1}{\epsilon}.$ An exact isotopy class of positive Lagrangian submanifolds admits a natural Riemannian metric. We prove that the Riemannian metric restricted to the subset of $\epsilon$-positive Lagrangians induces a path metric when the relative K\"ahler class of the ambient Calabi-Yau manifold lies on a line of rational slope. The proof relies on the construction of a sequence of quantization maps from a circle bundle over the space of positive Lagrangians to the dual of the space of holomorphic sections of powers of a prequantum line bundle. The rationality condition for the relative K\"ahler class allows us to reduce to the case of Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangians. Building on ideas of Tian and Nirenberg-Wells, H\"ormander estimates are used to show that functions on a Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangian can be approximated by holomorphic sections of a sufficiently high power of the prequantum line bundle. Consequently, the quantization maps eventually separate fibers of the circle bundle.
item.dc:creator: Jake P. Solomon, Bentzion Yavetz

item.title: On local minimality of Hausdorff dimension for round limit sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.20358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address a question of Canary--Taylor and Canary--Minsky--Taylor for sufficiently symmetric compact hyperbolic $3$-orbifolds with totally geodesic boundary. We give sufficient conditions on the symmetries of such an orbifold to show that, among the complete convex cocompact structures on the interior, the structure with Fuchsian ends is a critical point (respectively, a strict local minimum) for the critical exponent. We also provide an infinite family of non-rigid examples fulfilling these conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sami Douba, Andr\'es Sambarino, Franco Vargas Pallete

item.title: Deformations of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K. Broder, in the context of a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds equipped with a holomorphic family of holomorphic line bundles. Firstly, we show that the existence of a holomorphic $p$-contact structure is {\bf deformation-open} when a non-jumping assumption is made on the $\bar\partial$-cohomology of bidegree $(p,\,0)$. This ought to become a source of further examples of holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds. Secondly, we obtain a Berndtsson-type {\bf (semi-)positivity} result for the holomorphic vector bundle over the base induced, as a direct image, by the line bundle on the total space that supports the p-contact structures. Thirdly, we introduce a moduli space of relative holomorphic p-contact structures and we show that it is {\bf Hausdorff} and {\bf open} in a certain quotient topological space.
item.dc:creator: Dan Popovici

item.title: A Scale-Critical $\mu<\frac38$ Extension Principle for Spherically Symmetric Einstein-Scalar Field System
item.description: arXiv:2610.20468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a new quantitative, scale-critical $C^1$ extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. We derive estimates for solutions in the causal past of a possibly singular endpoint $\mathcal{O}$ of the center. Assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the Doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. We then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{O}$ provided the mass ratio $\mu=2m/r$ satisfies $\sup\mu<\frac38$. This improves the small-mass-ratio condition in Christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. Our proof has three new ingredients. First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. Third, we establish a family of higher-order Morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $\mu$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $\mu\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $\mu<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.
item.dc:creator: Xinliang An, Haoyang Chen, Jaydeep Singh

item.title: An extension principle for Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite Doppler exponent
item.description: arXiv:2610.20469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar field system. Rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in Christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in An--Chen--Singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by An-Tan [2] with finite Doppler exponent (blueshift). By conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $\alpha'$ with $\alpha'=\partial_v\alpha/\partial_vr$ and $\alpha=\partial_v(r\phi)/\partial_vr$. This provides the desired extension principle in An-Tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein. As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.
item.dc:creator: Xinliang An, Haoyang Chen, Taoran He

item.title: All Serrin bands are unduloidal
item.description: arXiv:2610.20581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that any Serrin domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with two boundary components is a member of the canonical unduloidal family
item.dc:creator: Laurent Hauswirth, Pablo Mira

item.title: Holography and Cheeger constant of asymptotically CMC submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2503.12703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(M^{n+1},g_+)$ be an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold. We compute the Cheeger constant of conformally compact asymptotically constant mean curvature submanifolds $ \iota : Y^{k+1} \to (M^{n+1},g_+)$ with arbitrary codimension. As an application, we provide two classes of examples of $(n+1)$-dimensional asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds with Cheeger constant equal to $n$, whose conformal infinity is of the following types: 1) positive Yamabe invariant, and 2) negative Yamabe invariant. Moreover, in the same spirit as Blitz--Gover--Waldron \cite{BlitzSamuel2021CFFa}, we show that an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold with umbilic boundary is conformally weakly Poincar\'e--Einstein if and only if the third conformal fundamental form of the boundary vanishes. Next, in the space of asymptotically minimal hypersurfaces $Y$ within a Poincar\'e--Einstein manifold, we identify an extrinsic conformal invariant of $\partial Y$ which obstructs the vanishing of the mean curvature of $Y$ to second order. This conformal invariant is a linear combination of two Riemannian hypersurface invariants of $\partial Y,$ one which depends on its extrinsic geometry within $\overline{Y}$ and the other on its extrinsic geometry within $\partial M;$ neither of which are conformal invariants individually. Finally, we show that for asymptotically minimal hypersurfaces with mean curvature vanishing to second order inside of a Poincar\'e--Einstein space, being weakly Poincar\'e--Einstein is equivalent to the boundary of $Y$ having vanishing second and third conformal fundamental forms when viewed as a hypersurface within the conformal infinity.
item.dc:creator: Samuel P\'erez-Ayala, Aaron J. Tyrrell

item.title: Lin-Lu-Yau Ricci curvature on hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2507.04109v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a unified framework for defining Lin-Lu-Yau (LLY) Ricci curvature on both undirected and directed hypergraphs. By establishing upper bounds and monotonicity properties for the parameterized curvature $\kappa_\alpha$, we justify the well-posedness and compatibility of our definitions. Furthermore, we prove a Bonnet-Myers-type theorem for hypergraphs, which highlights the potential of LLY Ricci curvature in hypergraph analysis, particularly in studying geometric and structural properties. Our results extends the foundational definitions of graph Ricci curvature by Ollivier and Lin-Lu-Yau to the hypergraph setting.
item.dc:creator: Yulu Tian, Liang Zhao

item.title: Characterizations of weak almost ${\mathcal S}$-manifolds with curvature properties
item.description: arXiv:2508.08871v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weak metric structures, introduced by Rovenski and Wolak in 2022, extend Yano's $f$-structure and almost contact metric structure. In this paper, we investigate curvature phenomena of weak almost ${\cal S}$-manifolds (w.a.$\,\cal S$-manifolds) focusing on the $f$-$(\kappa,\mu)$-nullity condition and its special case $R_{X,Y}\,\xi=0$. We establish several results that generalize known rigidity theorems for almost ${\cal S}$-manifolds. First, using the partial Ricci flow, we obtain dynamical characterizations of $\cal S$-manifolds: starting from a w.a.$\,\cal S$-structure satisfying the curvature condition of $\cal S$-manifolds or the $f$-$(1,\mu)$-nullity condition, the flow evolves the structure exponentially fast toward an $\cal S$-structure. This extends results of Cappelletti Montano and Di~Terlizzi to the weak metric setting. Next, we identify conditions under which a w.a.\,${\cal S}$-manifold admits a bi-Legendrian structure with totally geodesic foliations. Finally, for w.a.$\,\cal S$-manifolds with $\kappa=\mu=0$, we prove a splitting theorem in which one factor is flat and the another has positive constant sectional curvature, generalizing classical results for almost $\cal S$-geometry. These findings have consequences for the theory of Sasakian and $\cal S$- manifolds, the geometry of bi-Legendrian structures, and the behavior of weak metric contact manifolds under curvature constraints.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Nayak, Dhriti Sundar Patra, Vladimir Rovenski

item.title: All toric Hermitian ALE gravitational instantons
item.description: arXiv:2510.09291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the only smooth, Ricci flat, ALE gravitational instanton with a toric Hermitian non-K\"ahler structure is the Eguchi-Hanson instanton. The proof is analogous to the classification of toric Hermitian ALF instantons by Biquard and Gauduchon, although we avoid the use of toric K\"ahler geometry and instead perform a direct global analysis of the Tod form of the metric in Weyl-Papapetrou coordinates. This supports a conjecture by Gibbons and Bando-Kasue-Nakajima which states that any Ricci flat ALE instanton is self-dual.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo Araneda, James Lucietti

item.title: K\"ahler geometry on total spaces of vector bundles over elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2511.08906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study function theory and K\"ahler geometry on total spaces of vector bundles over an elliptic curve. Our main result characterizes the vector bundles whose total spaces admit complete K\"ahler metrics with nonnegative bisectional curvature ($BI \geq 0$ for short). We also obtain explicit expressions for all complete K\"ahler metrics with $BI \geq 0$ on the total space of a line bundle over a complex torus. These results are related to a general conjecture concerning the structure of complete K\"ahler manifolds with $BI \geq 0$. For rank-two vector bundles of degree zero over elliptic curves, we study holomorphic functions and automorphisms on the corresponding total spaces, and construct complete Gauduchon Hermitian metrics with vanishing Chern-Ricci curvature. These metrics are natural in the sense that the associated spaces of holomorphic functions of polynomial growth coincide with the ``polynomials'' on these total spaces.
item.dc:creator: Hanyu Wu, Bo Yang

item.title: Differential Invariants of Carrollian Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2606.30274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute invariants of Carrollian spacetimes, deriving them from the geometry of the screen bundle. For generic Carrollian structures we specify how to generate the entire algebra of differential invariants, with emphasis on dimension 3, which has special physical relevance. Then, in the framework of jet-spaces, we compute the numerology behind these invariants: the Hilbert and Poincar\'e functions that govern their numbers according to order. Finally, we compute the Spencer cohomology behind the Carrollian geometry that, in particular, contains the spaces of intrinsic torsion and intrinsic curvature, which are fundamental invariants, important in the equivalence problem and symmetry analysis. Thus, we also discuss symmetry sizes of Carrollian spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Boris Kruglikov, Eivind Schneider, Wijnand Steneker

item.title: Holomorphic functions on a class of complete Hermitian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2608.01594v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove a gradient estimate for holomorphic functions on complete Hermitian manifolds with nonnegative second Ricci curvature. As an application, we establish several Liouville-type theorems for holomorphic functions and mappings between complete Hermitian manifolds under suitable curvature assumptions. In particular, on a complete Hermitian manifold with nonnegative second Ricci curvature and Chern torsion of linear growth, any bounded holomorphic function must be constant. Moreover, we construct examples to show that both the gradient estimate and this Liouville theorem are sharp in a suitable sense. In the second part of the paper, we study holomorphic functions on simply connected complete Hermitian manifolds with vanishing Chern curvature and torsion norm of sublinear growth. Combining the gradient estimate with methods from sub-Riemannian geometry, we obtain a complete characterization of holomorphic functions of polynomial growth on such manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Zeqing Miao, Hanyu Wu, Bo Yang

item.title: Topology of tame contractible $n$-manifolds, $n=6,7$, with Positive BiRicci Curvature and Ricci lower bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.08686v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that if an open smooth $6$-manifold $M^6$ is the interior of a compact, contractible manifold with boundary $X^6$, such that $\pi_3(X,\partial X)=0$, and $M$ supports a complete metric with uniform positive BiRicci curvature and Ricci curvature bounded below, then $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^6$. Additionally, we show that if an open smooth $n$-manifold $M^n$, $n\in\{6,7\}$, is the interior of a compact, contractible manifold with boundary $X^n$, such that $\pi_3(X,\partial X)=0$, and $M$ supports a complete metric with positive BiRicci curvature with at most $C$-quadratic decay at infinity for some $C>C_n$ and nonnegative Ricci curvature, then $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^n$. Lastly, for each $n\geq6$, we construct a compact, contractible Newman $n$-manifold, $N^n$, based on a presentation of the Higman group such that $\pi_i(N,\partial N)=0$, $3\leq i \leq n-3$, and $\mathrm{int}(N)$ admits a complete metric with uniform positive scalar curvature and Ricci curvature bounded below.
item.dc:creator: Paul Sweeney Jr

item.title: Inverse limits of locally convex Lie groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2610.12296v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study strict inverse systems of locally convex Lie groupoids and Lie algebroids. We show that strict inverse limits of Lie algebroids and Lie groupoids inherit natural Lie structures and establish a natural isomorphism of functors $\varprojlim\circ\operatorname{Lie}\cong\operatorname{Lie}\circ\varprojlim$. We then consider inverse systems of integrable Banach-Lie algebroids and their source-simply connected levelwise integrations. We give conditions under which these integrations form a strict inverse system of Lie groupoids and hence their inverse limit integrates the inverse-limit algebroid. Under additional hypotheses on the source-fiber inverse sequence, we describe the obstruction to source-simply connectedness of the resulting integration in terms of the derived inverse limit $\varprojlim^{1}\pi_2$ of the second homotopy groups of the source fibers. We illustrate the theory with several examples: inverse limits of jet groupoids, current groupoids, and gauge groupoids, including the corresponding inverse-limit Atiyah algebroids and a source-simply connected inverse-limit integration arising from the quaternionic Hopf bundle.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Gamal Shaltut

item.title: $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-cohomology on multidifferential operators space
item.description: arXiv:2610.14820v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute cohomology spaces of the ortosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ on the (1,1)-dimensional real superspace with coefficients in the superspace $\frak{D}_{{\lambda},\mu}$ of $n$-ary differential operators acting on weighted densities (${\lambda}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mu\in\mathbb{R}$).
item.dc:creator: Mabrouk Ben Ammar, Amina Jabeur

item.title: Flexibility of eigenvalues for graph Laplacians arising from genus 3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.26308v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is known that the small eigenvalues of the Laplacian of a Riemann surface close to the boundary of the modular space can be well approximated by the eigenvalues of the discrete Laplacian on a certain graph coming from the pair of pants decomposition of the surface. In this paper, we provide a complete description of the sets of eigenvalues of the weighted graph Laplacian for all graphs on four vertices that correspond to a valid pair of pants decomposition of a surface of genus 3.
item.dc:creator: Alena Erchenko, Dmitry Jakobson, Allison Tsypin

item.title: Complex deformations of the circle: Group cohomology and Virasoro uniformization
item.description: arXiv:2605.20175v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We approach the question of complexification of the diffeomorphism group of the circle by considering real-analytic maps from the circle into the punctured complex plane with winding number +1. Such complex deformations form an infinite-dimensional manifold with partially defined inversion and composition operations, smooth in the sense of Fr\"olicher structures, and with Lie algebra relations at the identity given by the Witt algebra. We compute their second group cohomology with real coefficients. It is generated by two cocycles: One cocycle extending the Bott-Thurston cocycle related to the Gelf'and-Fuks cocycle of the Virasoro algebra, and another Euler class cocycle combining mean rotation and conformal radius. Complex deformations act naturally on the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces with enumerated and analytically parametrized boundary components, equipping them with smooth Fr{\"o}licher structures. We prove a Virasoro uniformization theorem: The tangent spaces of the Segal moduli spaces are spanned by vector fields induced by the Witt algebra. Finally, we relate the actions of complex deformations to Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates and Schiffer variation on finite-dimensional moduli spaces of bordered hyperbolic surfaces with one marked point on each boundary component.
item.dc:creator: Sid Maibach, Eveliina Peltola

item.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties I -klt Fano case-
item.description: arXiv:2607.25181v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish the following Miyaoka-Yau inequality for any $n$-dimensional klt Fano variety $X$, possibly K-unstable, in terms of its delta invariant: \[\left(2(n+1)\widehat{c}_2(X)-n c_1(X)^2\right)\cdot c_1(X)^{n-2} \ge -n \left(1-\min\{1,\delta(X)\}\right)^2 \cdot c_1(X)^n.\] Moreover, if equality holds in this inequality, then there exist a finite quasi-\'etale cover $\widehat{X} \to X$ and a positive integer $p$ such that $\widehat{X} \cong \mathbb{P}(1,\ldots, 1, p)$. We also discuss the relationship between Donaldson's conjecture and the Miyaoka-Yau inequality.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Hisamoto, Masataka Iwai

item.title: Regularization and H\"older continuity for complex Hessian equations on Hermitian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2608.15552v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold, and let $\Gamma$ be a symmetric convex cone. We develop a quantitative regularization method for $\Gamma$-admissible functions. As an application, we prove H\"older continuity for every pluripotential solution of complex $m$-Hessian equations whose right-hand sides belong to $L^p$, for $p>\frac{n}{m}$. These results extend to a more general class of complex Hessian equations satisfying the structural condition used by Guo--Phong--Tong.
item.dc:creator: Yulun Xu

item.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersection in flag varieties
item.description: arXiv:2609.21914v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a root-theoretic localization formalism for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of flag varieties and of smooth zero loci of globally generated homogeneous vector bundles. The resulting invariants are expressed as finite sums over decorated trees whose contributions are determined by the root system of the ambient flag variety and by the torus weights of the defining bundle. We connect these computations with the Theory of Hodge Atoms of Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu via the matrix of small quantum multiplication by first Chern class. Let $X$ be a Fano fourfold with $h^{3,1}(X)=1$ arising as a hyperplane section of a suitable Fano fivefold. Its cohomology decomposes into a monodromy-fixed part and the middle vanishing cohomology. This decomposition is preserved by quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. Moreover, it acts by a scalar on the vanishing summand. We show, for the monodromy-fixed block, that (a) if every eigenvalue has algebraic multiplicity at most two and $X$ is Hodge general, then $X$ is irrational; (b) if every eigenvalue has Jordan defect at most one and $X$ is rational, then every weak factorization contains a smooth surface center whose minimal model is a projective K3 surface. Many applications are presented. Using the recently introduced quantum connection approach to irrationality, we obtain from the computations here presented the irrationality of the very general smooth complete intersection of a hyperplane and a quadric in $\operatorname{LG}(3,6)$; the very general smooth quadric section in $G_2/P_2$; and the very general smooth complete intersection of five hyperplanes and a quadric in the spinor 10-fold.
item.dc:creator: Boris Alexeev, Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Giovane Galindo, Bogdan Georgiev, Ludmil Katzarkov, Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins
